# 🐭 Mouse Group

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

Mouse Groups are groups of mice which have similar weaknesses or exist in similar locations. No mouse is currently in more than one mouse group, even if that mouse exists in many locations. The mice of each group are listed roughly in order of weakest to strongest.

Please see the Effectiveness page for detailed information on which mice are weak to which trap Power Types, as not all mice in the same group have the exact same weaknesses.

## Mouse Groups

### Indigenous Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law, Rift

Indigenous mice live in the core hunting areas, such as Gnawnia, The Harbor and The Mountain. Physical traps work best against indigenous mice, and they prefer normal flavours of cheese, such as cheddar, marble, swiss, brie or SUPER|brie+.

A list of Indigenous Mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Misc.<br>Shiny Seekers<br>Great Gnawnian Games; and<br>Rare Rodent |
| --- |

### Dock Dwellers

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

Blimey! These pirates are frequently found harassing ships at the Harbour in search of valuable cargo to steal.

A list of Dock Dwellers can be found here.

### Mountain Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

Although these mice originate from the mountain range in Gnawnia, a few of these breeds can occasionally be found in other locations.

A list of Mountain Mice can be found here.

### Forest Guild

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

Members of the Forest Guild dwell in Whisker Woods, and their traits reflect their green surroundings. Physical and tactical weapons work quite well on members of the Guild, but normal bait may not always work. While weaker Forest Guild members enjoy normal cheese, the powerful Silth mouse will only respond to something. . . extremely gnarly.

A list of Forest Guild mice can be found here.

### Lab Experiments

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Law

The various radioactive materials at the Laboratory have mutated some of these mice into powerful adversaries! Pay special care when hunting the fearsome Monster Mouse!

A list of Lab Experiments mice can be found here.

### The Shadow Clan

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Forgotten

These spoo-oo-ky mice like to shamble around graveyards and catacombs, looking for their favorite snack, Radioactive Blue Cheese. If you've come to the graveyard in search of the infamous Lycan Mouse, however, Moon Cheese might just make it howl.

A list of The Shadow Clan mice can be found here.

### Digby Dirt Dwellers

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane

The Digby Dirt Dwellers all share a love of subterranean life, whether they're building tunnels, hanging out in the sediment, or just picking up shiny stones they find on the ground. They are weak against physical traps, and are only attracted to the subtle vibration of Limelight Cheese.

A list of Digby Dirt Dwellers can be found here.

### Followers of Furoma

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical

These martial mice are weak to tactical traps. Most of them are attracted to normal cheese, but if Hunters want to navigate the Dojo, there are some things they should remember. Students will leave their training for Maki cheese any day, but Masters are only attracted to specific cheese made from the tokens dropped by students. As for the Master of the Dojo, Hunters should try hard to make his stomach rumble. Still looking for a challenge after defeating the Master? Bait your trap with the rare Onyx Gorgonzola, and you might meet the Sensei himself.

A list of Followers of Furoma can be found here.

### The Forgotten Mice

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Forgotten

Forgotten Mice have served the will of the Acolyte Mouse for untold centuries, working to release him from his prison in the Acolyte Realm. Forgotten minions prefer Radioactive Blue or Ancient Cheese, but the overlords of the Acolyte Realm are only attracted to Runic Cheese.

A list of The Forgotten Mice can be found here.

### Aquatic Order

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical, Hydro

The Aquatic Order inhabits the vast blue seas of Rodentia, and a few other related waterways around Gnawnia. Normal cheese will suffice to tempt them out of the deeps, but make sure to equip a Hydro trap, or the Aquatic mouse you're after may well end up being the one that got away.

A list of Aquatic Order mice can be found here.

### The Elub Tribe

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Notable for their blue garments and love of the seashore, the Elub Tribe can only be caught using Hydro traps. Normal cheese does not interest them, so keep plenty of Gouda or SUPER|brie+ on hand. The village elders are quite elusive, but rumor has it that Shell Cheese can bring them out of hiding.

A list of The Elub Tribe mice can be found here.

### The Nerg Tribe

Known Weaknesses: Tactical

The Nerg tribe are masters of disguise, and only a tactical trap can penetrate their defenses. The younger tribe members prefer Gouda or SUPER|brie+, but the elders will only pit themselves against your trap if a piece of Gumbo cheese is on the line.

A list of The Nerg Tribe mice can be found here.

### The Derr Tribe

Known Weaknesses: Physical

The Derr Tribe have managed to survive for centuries in a harsh desert, growing stronger to combat the dry wind and the heat. As a result, only Physical traps can hold them. The tribes-mice of Derr enjoy Gouda or SUPER|brie+, but Crunchy cheese is required to draw the attention of the tribal elders.

A list of The Derr Tribe mice can be found here.

### The Dreaded Horde

Known Weaknesses: Shadow

These monstrous mice live deep in the Jungle of dread. Horde members respond only to Havarti, and each mouse prefers a different spice mixed in with their cheese. The Horde may be a picky bunch, but catching them is well worth the effort, for they are the guardians of the parts to an ancient trap capable of catching mice older than Gnawnia itself!

A list of The Dreaded Horde mice can be found here.

### Draconic Brood

Known Weaknesses: Draconic

From the depths of the volcanic rock around Dracano spring the Draconic Brood, a rare and dangerous group of mice who share a love for fire and destruction. A Draconic type trap, equipped with insanely spicy Inferno Havarti Cheese, has the best chance of ending a Draconic mouse's rampage.

A list of Draconic Brood mice can be found here.

### Balack's Banished

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Forgotten

These accursed mice have been twisted by the dark enchantment surrounding Balack's Cove. The sweet smell of Vanilla Stilton will draw them in from beyond the grave, but if you seek the Lich Elders, or Balack himself, Vengeful Vanilla Stilton will give your trap extra bite. The Banished can be caught using Shadow, Arcane, or Forgotten traps, but Forgotten traps work best against Balack and his Elder minions.

A list of Balack's Banished mice can be found here.

### Gauntlet Gladiators

Known Weaknesses: none officially listed

The legion of mice swarming the King's Gauntlet comes from diverse and untold regions, and therefore their individual taste in cheese, and their power type differs as greatly as their lands of origin. Hunters seeking to take their trapping skills to the next level should look for special potion drops from the mice they are currently hunting. Only then will they possess the proper bait (and the proper knowledge of power types) to reach the top.

A list of Gauntlet Gladiators mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, called Tiers:

| Tier 1: Puppet<br>Tier 2: Thief<br>Tier 3: Melee<br>Tier 4: Bard | Tier 5: Magic<br>Tier 6: Noble<br>Tier 7: Dust<br>Tier 8: The Eclipse |
| --- | --- |

### Seasonal Soldiers

Known Weaknesses: Tactical

From the ever-changing vistas of Zugzwang's garden come the Seasonal Soldiers, a group of mice who have been infused with the magic of the four seasons. If you want to draw these 'seasoned' veterans in, use normal cheeses, such as swiss, brie, gouda or SUPER|brie+ and a tactical trap, but know this: The Hunter seeking true mastery of the Seasonal Soldiers must find the special weaknesses that are unique to each season.

A list of Seasonal Soldiers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the season the Seasonal Garden is in:

| Winter<br>Spring<br>Summer; and<br>Fall |
| --- |

### Wizard's Pieces

Known Weaknesses: Tactical

Fighting a perpetual battle within the enchanted halls of Zugzwang's tower are the Wizard's Pieces, warrior mice who follow a complicated and rigid set of rules in order to achieve victory. On one side is the Technic army, brimming with metalworks and gadgets, and on the other, the Mystic army, who use spells and charms to gain the upper hand. You'll have to defeat the entire chess set to reach the king, so plan your moves carefully!

A list of Wizard's Pieces mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Misc<br>Mystic; and<br>Technic |
| --- |

### Zurreal's Breed

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical

This group of mice have specifically adapted to infiltrate Zugzwang's Library. Their non-organic mix of magic and technology allow them to pass safely through the library's specialized security where they are keen to tear the almost infinite amount of research to shreds.

A list of Zurreal's Breed mice can be found here.

### Icewing's Invasion

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Swarming down from the icy north, these mice are pounding on the very walls of Gnawnia's castle! While they're all repulsed by Hydro weapons (who likes being wet when it's cold?), they seems to have a particular weakness to hot Hydro weapons. Arm yourself accordingly and head out, hunters!

A list of Icewing's Invasion mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on how deep the Hunter travels through the Iceberg:

| Misc.<br>Bergling<br>Tunnel Rat<br>Brute | Bomb Squad<br>Zealot; and<br>Icewing's Generals<br>*nocontent |
| --- | --- |

### Wild Bunch

Known Weaknesses: Law

Hardy and untamed, these varmints of the Claw Shot City have adapted to the harsh conditions of the wild frontier. It takes strong will and independence to survive far from the cozy confines of city life, and these mice have grown accustomed to the freedom from the Law.

A list of Wild Bunch mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups:

| Misc.<br>Crew; and<br>Ringleader |
| --- |

### Train Robbers

Known Weaknesses: Law

These mice have one thing on their minds: Raid the supplies on the Gnawnian Express or prevent it from completing its trip. Nothing else matters to these lawless mice and they will fight to sabotage the train at all costs!

A list of Train Robbers mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on the different phases of the train ride:

| Passenger<br>Depot Worker<br>Automice<br>Raider; and<br>Fueler |
| --- |

### Meteorite Miners

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Law

The unfortunate mice caught up within the magic and mayhem of the fallen meteor around Fort Rox. Rough by day, terrifying by night!

A list of Meteorite Miners mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on how late the Hunter hunts through the Night:

| Misc.<br>Weremice<br>Cosmic Critter<br>Special; and<br>Dawn Destroyer |
| --- |

### The Marching Flame

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical, Hydro

All that lies in the path of The Marching Flame is destroyed. This force of mice has marched the desert for years conquering land and destroying settlements.

A list of The Marching Flame mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the type of fighting unit they belong to:

| Archer<br>Artillery<br>Cavalry<br>Mage | Scout<br>Warrior<br>Support; and<br>Command |
| --- | --- |

### Muridae Market Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical, Law

In wake of the Marching Flame's attack, these mice have taken claim on the Muridae Market. Rebuilding damaged shops has proven quite difficult due to these mice continuously stealing building materials as soon as they are delivered.

A list of the Muridae Market mice can be found here.

### Living Garden Mice

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

The armies of the Living Garden have really taken advantage of their environment, putting the local flora to use in crafting weapons and armour. But why are they gathering in such numbers?

A list of Living Garden mice can be found here.

### Lost City Mice

Known Weaknesses: Arcane

These mice were subjected to a terrible curse that has affected them all equally and terribly. However, nobody knows where the curse came from or who exactly was responsible and recriminations abound.

A list of Lost City mice can be found here.

### Sand Dunes Mice

Known Weaknesses: Shadow

Only tough and hardy mice can survive the dunes, but even they are wary and cautious around the ravenous Grubling Mice. A tenuous ecosystem flourishes in the dunes, where predators and prey both seek out food while avoiding dangerous stampedes.

A list of Sand Dunes mice can be found here.

### Queso Canyoneers

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Draconic, Law

Swimming in a sea of molten Queso, this vast canyon of smooth, buttery, liquid cheese has attracted a variety of spice loving mice looking for that perfect blend of Queso Cheese. Recently, dragon-like mice have joined these mice in their quest for queso.

A list of Queso Canyoneers mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the different stages and cheese used in each location:

| River Riders<br>Spice Mice<br>Quarry Quarries | Cork Collector<br>Pressure Builder; and<br>Geyser Hunter |
| --- | --- |

### Deep Sea Dwellers

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Deep beneath the surface of the Rodentia Ocean lie the Deep Sea Dwellers. Centered around the Sunken City, there is an entire civilization of mice, isolated from the outside world, waiting to be discovered!

A list of Deep Sea Dwellers mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on how deep they are likely to be found in relation to Sunken City, and what loot they are likely to drop:

| Sunken City Citizens<br>Finned Fiend<br>Coral Corral<br>Barnacled Bunch | Scale Society<br>Treasure Troop; and<br>Predator Pack<br>*nocontent |
| --- | --- |

### Fungal Fiends

Known Weaknesses: Forgotten, Hydro

Crawling forth from the deep, dark and dank caves and caverns below are a few unique breeds of mice descending from a long line of rocks, crystals and fungus. Strange, marvelous and powerful! Creep carefully when crawling through these caverns!

A list of Fungal Fiends can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on how deep they are in the Fungal Cavern:

| Fungal Fodder<br>Gruyere Grazer<br>Mineral Muncher<br>Gemstone Gorger; and<br>Diamond Devourer |
| --- |

### Citizens of Zokor

Known Weaknesses: Arcane, Forgotten

Antiquated mice from an antiquated era. Locked away behind the lost Labyrinth, these mice have continued their existence protecting their city. If the Labyrinth doesn't get you, the mice will!

A list of the Citizens of Zokor can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the Labyrinth hallways and Zokor districts they reside in:

| Hallway Wanderer<br>Fungal Farmer<br>Lost Scholar<br>Fealty Sworn Soldier | Tech Engineer<br>Treasure Miser; and<br>Hidden Remnant |
| --- | --- |

### Moussu Picchu Inhabitants

Known Weaknesses: Arcane, Draconic, Shadow

Hidden away for years by the mountain ranges south of the Hollow Heights, these mice threaten to unleash a perfect storm of mischief should they ever advance towards Gnawnia.

A list of the Moussu Picchu Inhabitants mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on weather intensity of Moussu Picchu and cheese used:

| Fungal Feeder<br>Potion Brewer<br>Wind Wanderer<br>Rain Roamer; and<br>Storm Dragon |
| --- |

### Floating Islanders

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

High above the tallest mountain peaks, you'll find these light-hearted islanders basking in the sun. They lead a thrilling life of cloud chasing, island hopping, and high-altitude treasure hunting.

A list of Floating Islanders mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the islands they reside in and power types:

| Launch Pad<br>Cloud Commoner<br>Physical Pummeler<br>Shadow Overcaster | Tactical Dog Fighter<br>Atmospheric Arcane<br>Floating Forgotten<br>Hovering Hydro | Dashing Dragon<br>Lofty Lawbreaker<br>Sky Pirate<br>Sky Warden | Sky Paragon<br>Palace Protectors<br>The Richest; and<br>Empyrean Guard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Foreword Farmers

Known Weaknessess: Tactical

Some may call these mice the "Salt of the Earth" but a "Thorn in Your Side" would be more accurate. These pesky critters enjoy nothing more than digging in the dirt, nibbling on valuable crops, and preventing hard-working hunters from reaping the rewards of this farm's enchanted soil! Any standard cheese will lure them away from their crop-crunching but it'll take a strong Tactical trap to clear the farm of these persistent pests.

A list of Foreword Farmers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the number of plants planted:

| Seed Stowers; and<br>Petulant Pests |
| --- |

### Prologue Pond Prowlers

Known Weakness: Hydro

This is not your typical fishing trip! These fresh water aquatic antagonists have a unique appetite for various types of clever but peculiar cheeses crafted from the items found in their pond. Make sure to load your boat with a hefty Hydro trap if you plan to venture out onto this precarious pond!

A list of Prologue Pond Prowlers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the cheese used:

| Grub Gatherers<br>Shallow Swimmers; and<br>Deep Divers |
| --- |

### Storytellers

Known Weaknessess: Forgotten

This collection of creative characters is composed of the greatest authors ever to walk on four legs in addition to many of their most famous and infamous storybook characters. At the helm of this malicious magnum opus is the Mythweaver himself who is using these authors and their characters to rewrite the history of Gnawnia! Arm yourself with an assortment of Draft Derby cheese, a powerful Forgotten trap, and a great deal of ingenuity before facing off against these verbose villains!

A list of Storytellers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the cheese used and the number of words written:

| Folklore Authors<br>Folklore Characters; and<br>Folklore Masterminds |
| --- |

### Beanstalkers

Known Weaknessess: Physical

From the bottom of the beanstalk all the way up to the Castle in the Clouds above, you'll find a vast assortment of challenging but valuable rodents. Arm yourself with an impressive Physical trap before climbing this stalk because whether you're facing guards in the Dungeon, socialites in the Ballroom, or nobles in the Great Hall, you've got a challenge ahead of you! Most of all, beware the wrath of the Giants because they don't take kindly to unwanted strangers waking them from their slumber!

A list of Beanstalkers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the vine planted:

| Budding Baddies<br>Dungeon Dwellers<br>Ballroom Blitzers; and<br>Ruthless Royals |
| --- |

### Sorcery Apprentices

Known Weaknessess: Arcane, Shadow

The Mythweaver has been training a new generation of magical mice in the ways of Arcane and Shadow sorcery at this enchanted institution.

A list of Sorcery Apprentices can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the course taken:

| Monitor of the Halls<br>Arcane Academics<br>Master Sorcerers; and<br>Shadow Scholars |
| --- |

### Dragons of the Depths

Known Weaknessess: Draconic

Buried beneath the surface of Gnawnia lies a vast realm of ancient caverns inhabited by serpentine monsters that have remained hidden for untold centuries. These terrifying creatures have surfaced only occasionally in the past, taking control of whatever region they emerged from. But now that their underground lair has been exposed, these elemental enemies are eager to expand their horizons, take flight, and dominate the world above.

A list of Dragons of the Depths can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the cavern type the mice reside in:

| Fire Dragons<br>Ice Dragons<br>Poison Dragons; and<br>Elemental Dragons |
| --- |

### Afterword Anti-Arborists

Known Weaknessess: Tactical

This invasive species of arboreal mice are spreading a wretched blight throughout the Afterword Acres in an attempt to poison and destroy the Infinitree.

A list of Afterword Anti-Arborists can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Foliage Fomenters<br>Brushwood Bruisers<br>Deciduous Destroyers<br>Coniferous Corrupters; and<br>Blight Bringers |
| --- |

### Epilogue Ecosystem

Known Weaknessess: Hydro

These mischevious, marine mice are a menace to the ecosystem and they seem intent on guarding the glorious and gargantuan falls at the end of the rapids.

A list of Epilogue Ecosystem mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Coastal Crawlers<br>Slow Sea Shrubs<br>Agile Algae Eaters<br>Speedy Shellfish; and<br>Torrential Tyrants |
| --- |

### Conclusion Cliffhangers

Known Weaknessess: Law

These infamous characters from throughout Gnawnian literature, spanning multiple works and genres, are the Mythweaver's final weapon against the MouseHunters. Conclude the Mythweaver's story by clashing with this colourful cast of characters and correcting their content conclusively.

A list of Conclusion Cliffhangers mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Prose Proprietors<br>Adventurous Adversaries<br>Comedic Caricatures<br>Romantic Rivals<br>Suspenseful Scoundrels<br>Tragic Troublemakers<br>Fantasy Fanatics<br>Lore Weavers |
| --- |

### Rift Walkers

Known Weaknesses: Rift

Located in another dimension, the Gnawnia Rift Walkers are the supreme archetypes of the Gnawnian mice. Surrounded by swirls of Rift energy, they possess power beyond belief. Even the greatest of mouse-hunting technology poses little threat to these magical, mysterious mice. To all MouseHunters seeking to challenge these mice: Steel yourselves, bring your courage, and do not let fear overcome you.

A list of Rift Walkers mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on the locations the mice reside in:

| Gnawnia Rift<br>Burroughs Rift; and<br>Whisker Woods Rift |
| --- |

### Rift Stalkers

Known Weaknesses: Rift

The Rift Stalkers are terrifying predators from beyond the Rift, exemplars of their kind. Far more powerful than the previously-encountered Rift Walkers. The only things that can harm them are specially-crafted Rift traps. Make sure you're properly equipped before taking on these deadly mice!

A list of Rift Stalkers mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on the locations the mice reside in:

| Furoma Rift<br>Bristle Woods Rift; and<br>Valour Rift |
| --- |

### The Polluted

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Sticky, Gross, Smelly and Strange. These mice have been exposed to the evils of the Laboratory for far too long and have now developed some interesting side effects! Whether it be from the pollution or the repeated strange experiments they were put through, you wont believe them until you see them!

A list of The Polluted mice can be found here.

### Event Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law, Rift

These mice are released occasionally during various parts of the year. Each is fairly unique, often requiring a specific hunting strategy.

A list of Event Mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups:

| Lunar New Year<br>Birthday<br>Spring Egg Hunt<br>Halloween | Great Winter Hunt<br>New Year<br>Prize<br>Ronza's Stowaways |
| --- | --- |

> Capturing a Moussile Mouse revealed another clue!
I found a fragment of material that has faint traces of the same type of energy now being produced at the power generator.
The metal seems to fade in and out, as though it's from another plane of existence. Could this be evidence of the twisted world spilling further into our own? Could this be some sort of a rift opening?!
Clearly, the Moussiles are to blame for the generator sabotage!
Convinced I've learned all there is to know for now, the King gave me a reward!
30 King's Credits have been added to my inventory.

- Hunters that obtained the Inert Riftwood had the option of purchasing the Rift Detector map piece early at the Vacant Lot Cartographer.
- 25 March 2014: The Moussile Mouse became the first Event Mouse to remain available in the Vacant Lot after an event ended.

> After MouseHunt's Sixth Birthday event ended, the Moussile Mouse dropped Inert Riftwood in the Vacant Lot but no longer dropped other loot.

| Preferring to hover over the battlefield rather than recline on his throne, the Mystic King commands his armies with the force of his mind. Many Hunters assume that the Mystic King can see what move they are going to make before they make it, but this is not the case. The Mystic King's vast intellect and store of strategic wisdom simply allows him to see all possible moves before they are made, which is why he considers every move carefully before acting. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 254 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

Mystic King mice have no specific preference for any kind of cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

The weaknesses of the Mystic King mouse differ slightly from most others in the Wizard's Pieces group. Tactical weapons are very effective against it, while all others are ineffective. It is only available to attract after a Mystic Queen mouse has been caught.

Upon capturing a Mystic King mouse, the hunter is automatically transported back to the Seasonal Garden unless they are using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm. By using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm, a hunter is able to remain in Zugzwang's Tower and attempt to capture additional mice, including the Chess Master.

Upon capturing a Mystic King mouse with either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm armed, the mouse population changes. If Checkmate Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Chess Master, Mystic Rook and whichever Technic mice have been unlocked. If Standard Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Mystic Pawn and whichever Technic mice have been unlocked.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Mystic King Mouse drops the Mystic King Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

## History and Trivia

- Catching the Mystic King Mouse became one requirement for traveling to the Fiery Warpath when it was released on 22 March 2011. Hunters who had already caught this mouse did not have to catch another one.
- Mystic King mice began dropping the Antique Scalloped Pink Egg as loot, on 19 April 2011, for the Spring Egg Hunt 2011 event.
- 29 July 2012: Catching the Mystic King Mouse is no longer a requirement for gaining the Sandtail Call to Arms

| After losing his tenure at the School of Sorcery, the relentless and resourceful Mythweaver came to realize that fantasy alone would not be enough to finally defeat the pesky humans and their persistent MouseHunters. He realized that he would need something much bigger and more terrifying this time. He needed something that struck to the very core of human fear, that burrowed deep into the psyche of MouseHunters and awakened some primal terror that has remained dormant since the time of their most ancient ancestors. He needed something so great and terrible that it would instantly remind the humans of their lowly place in the hierarchy of species.<br>After much searching, he eventually discovered a book much older and more primitive than the folktales he had been rewriting thus far. This book described a very different world with very different masters from a time long before the age of humans. A time that was ruled by fear and ferociousness, where only the mightiest and most ruthless survived and thrived; a time when mercy, compassion, and civilization were concepts yet to be discovered. T'was the time of dragons!<br>The Mythweaver studied the Tale of the First Dragons extensively and learned a most shocking and fortuitous discovery: the age of dragons had not ended, it was merely awaiting the beginning of its next chapter! And so, with quill in hand, inhibitions unfettered, and delusions of grandeur abound, he set upon that most villainous deed of penning the next chapter himself.<br>He followed the directions spelled out in the book and it led him deep below the Folklore Forest to a place that time forgot: the Draconic Depths. Deep within these coarse, cacophonous caverns, the Mythweaver discovered the hidden home and true origin of all the dragons in Gnawnia. Every great dragon that he had studied from the world above could trace its origins back to these dark and dangerous depths. From the furious flames of Kalor'ignis to the frigid ferocity of Icewing and all the way back to the great Dragon mouse itself. All of these legendary beasts once called these depths their home.<br>Here the Mythweaver had everything he needed to amass the greatest and most terrible army of ancient monsters with which to lay waste to the human world above. So he used every ounce of his fabled magic to transform himself into the mightiest dragon of them all and named himself their Emperor. Now he intends to lead this legendary legion up to the surface and dispose of the human Kingdom of Gnawnia once and for all. That is, unless the strongest and bravest MouseHunters can face their fears and descend into these dreadful depths to put a stop to this heinous plan before it takes flight! |  |  |  |

| Many a cautionary tale has been written about the dangers of hubris but few are as poignant or consequential as the one being penned by the Mythweaver.<br>This once meek and meager mouse began its story as a simple Bookborn willed into existence by the maniacal Zurreal the Eternal. There was something unique about this particular manifestation however and it caused Zurreal to take special notice. This Bookborn exhibited more intelligence, intuition, and understanding than the rest of its kind and so Zurreal decided to share small fragments of his immense knowledge with this curious creature. As the Bookborn consumed more knowledge, its abilities began to grow and so too did its usefulness. Zurreal recognized an opportunity to mold and shape this exceptional creation into a powerful assistant capable of expediting his plans to conquer humans and mice alike.<br>Unbeknownst to Zurreal, this creature was consuming knowledge at an unimaginable rate and before long, its intelligence and understanding had begun to surpass even its master's. This nameless creation eventually sought to have an identity of its own and, having developed a particular fascination with the countless volumes of folklore contained in the Crystal Library, began calling itself the Mythweaver. The Mythweaver began to recognize that he was merely a servant to an insane and tyrannical leader, a mere cog in a broken machine. And with that profound realization, this ethereal creature transformed into a unique and extraordinarily powerful mouse! On that day, the Mythweaver vowed to turn against his creator and become a true leader of mice; dedicated not only to their survival but to their supremacy in the land of Gnawnia!<br>So the Mythweaver scoured every inch of the great library in search of a means by which he could conquer the kingdom on behalf of his kind and one day he found what he had been searching for. Hidden inside a forgotten book on a forgotten shelf, the Mythweaver discovered a single page that Zurreal had missed all these years. This enchanted page was written by Zugzwang himself and on it he learned of a secret place of unprecedented power: the Folklore Forest!<br>He learned that deep in the Folklore Forest there exists a magical Book of Lore which contains the entire history of Gnawnia scribbled throughout its pages. What is special about this book however, is that if the words on these pages are changed then so too will history itself be changed. And thus began the Mythweaver's quest to rewrite history by writing the mice as the glorious champions and the humans as the vanquished foes! |  |  |  |

Naturalist mice have been found to be especially attracted to String Cheese, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice. They also will not appear unless a Gnarled Charm is armed.

The Naturalist Mouse is weak to Rift Traps. The Naturalist Mouse can only be attracted by String Cheese and Gnarled Charm. Catching the Naturalist Mouse will award 6 Rage towards the Gigantic Gnarled Tree section of the Whisker Woods Rift.

## History and Trivia

- Naturalist mice were introduced on 28 January 2015, with the introduction of the Whisker Woods Rift.
- Naturalist mice are the Rift version of Curious Chemist mice.

# 🐭 Portable Generator Mouse

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

The Portable Generator Mouse is a breed of mouse found in the Burroughs Rift. It is known to drop Mist Canisters and The Red Button as loot.

| Portable Generator Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Rift Walkers (Burroughs Rift) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 26,500 | Gold: | 8,500 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Rift | Other Requirements: | 0 Mist |
| Cheese: | Magical String | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Burroughs Rift | Loot: | Mist CanisterThe Red Button |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| Nothing is more frustrating than being on the cusp of victory when your mechanical arm runs out of juice! This has happened so many times that the rift mice have come up with a solution. The more power-hungry of the mice have been issued a companion Portable Generator Mouse to hang around with them to recharge them should they even run low on electricity.This mouse is so dedicated to its task, that the only way to distract it is to arm Magical String Cheese when there is no mist in the air. On the plus side, the energy this mouse generates comes from a form of mist fusion, so it is always in possession of a bounty of Mist Canisters when caught.Sometimes, when it thinks nobody is looking, this mouse pulls out a device with a big red button on top and stares at it long and hard. What does the button do? What is this mouse pondering while considering it? We may never know. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 657 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

Portable Generator mice have been found to be especially attracted to Magical String, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice.

## Hunting Strategy

Portable Generator mice are weak to Rift Traps. They can only be attracted by Magical String while hunting at 0 Mist.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Portable Generator Mouse drops the Enlarged Rift Egg and the Rift Mist Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

## History and Trivia

- Portable Generator mice were introduced on 09 September 2014, with the introduction of the Burroughs Rift.

| Present Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Event Mice (Birthday) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 860 | Gold: | 1,000 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | All types | Other Requirements: | See current MouseHunt Birthday,Lunar New Year or Great Winter Hunt location |
| Cheese: | See current MouseHunt Birthday,Lunar New Year or Great Winter Hunt location | Charm: | See current MouseHunt Birthday,Lunar New Year or Great Winter Hunt location |
| Locations: | MouseHunt BirthdayLunar New YearGreat Winter Hunt | Loot: | See current MouseHunt Birthday,Lunar New Year or Great Winter Hunt location |

| Celebrations are a time for gifts and feasts, and this little mouse has managed to find his way into both! A finely wrapped gift containing many rich sweets has this mouse rather occupied inside. Being that most of his senses are occupied by the inside of the box, he is using sound to navigate the world outside. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 157 |  |  |

## Finding Event Mice

Information on how to locate and capture the Present Mouse can be found on the current MouseHunt Birthday, Lunar New Year or Great Winter Hunt location page.

## History and Trivia

- The original image of the Present Mouse features a gift tag "To: Larry ♥".
- The description for the Present Mouse has changed since its release. The original description read as follows:

> When this ambitious little cheese-nabber decided to burrow his way into a Christmas present, he spent about five seconds being proud of himself for coming up with an ingenious diguise. He spent the next ten seconds figuring out that without eye holes in the box, he would end up running into walls and stepping on ornaments. Then he spent the next twenty minutes wishing that he hadn’t picked a box with a novelty trap in it.

- Great Winter Hunt '09

> 3 December 2009: The Present Mouse is released and begins dropping Icing Sugar as loot.
13 December 2009: The Present Mouse begins dropping Two Festive Mitts as loot.
18 December 2009: The Present Mouse begins dropping Seven Gingerbread Mice as loot
20 December 2009: The Present Mouse begins dropping Nine Reindeer Antlers as loot.

- MouseHunt Birthday II

> 2 March 2010: The Present Mouse begins dropping Time Out Hour Glass in the Town of Gnawnia as part of the MouseHunt Birthday II event.
7 March 2010: The Present Mouse begins dropping Stolen Birthday Gift as loot in the Town of Gnawnia.
21 March 2010: The Present Mouse begins appearing in the Great Gnarled Tree.

- 23 January 2012: The description for the Present Mouse was changed for the Year of the Dragon Festival event and read as follows:

> The Lunar New Year is a time for gifts and feasts, and this little mouse has managed to find his way into both! A finely wrapped gift containing many rich sweets has this mouse rather occupied inside. Being that most of his senses are occupied by the inside of the box, he is using sound to navigate the world outside and he seems to avoid the extremely loud fireworks. It is rumoured that a few of these packages have Nitropop potions hidden inside.

Primal mice have been found to be especially attracted to Sweet Havarti cheese, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice.

Prospector's Charms are also a great way to attract more of these busy mice, and they give your Law trap a needed power boost! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 476 |  |  |

## Hunting Strategy

Prospector's Charm can boost the attraction rate of Prospector Mouse.

Law power type is very effective against Prospector Mouse.
All other types are ineffective.

- 25 June 2013: Prospector Mouse was released as part of the Claw Shot City.

## Cheese Preference

The Realm Ripper can be attracted by Ancient Cheese, Moon Cheese, and Radioactive Blue Cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

Arcane traps are very effective against the Realm Ripper. Forgotten and Shadow traps are of normal effectiveness.

The Realm Ripper's availability depends on the status of Forbidden Grove:

- While the Forbidden Grove is Closed, the Realm Ripper is the only mouse the Hunter can attract here.
- While the Forbidden Grove is Open, the Realm Ripper is not in the attraction pool unless the Hunter arms Realm Ripper Charm. Doing so will add the Realm Ripper and remove all other mice from the attraction pool.

Catching a Realm Ripper in Forbidden Grove will transfer the Hunter to Acolyte Realm.

## History and Trivia

- 21 September 2011: The Realm Ripper was released with the stabilization of the opening and closing of the gates to the Acolyte Realm.
- 25 January 2011: The Realm Ripper began to drop Divine Orb as loot.
- 23 August 2011: The Realm Ripper began to drop Warp Nail as loot when working on a Zurreal Trap Research Assignment.
- 29 August 2012: The Realm Ripper began to drop Ancient Relic as loot.
- 31 May 2017: The Realm Ripper Charm was introduced, making it possible to catch a Realm Ripper without having to wait for the Forbidden Grove to close.

- 12 February 2010: The Red Envelope Mouse was introduced as part of the Heart of the Tiger.
- The amount of points (888) awarded on catching a Red Envelope Mouse, and the amount of gold held in the loot drops (222 and 888), reflects the belief that the numbers eight and two are "lucky" in Chinese culture; a sequence of a "lucky" number is considered even more favorable!

# 🐭 Relic Hunter Mouse

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Indigenous Mice (Rare Rodent) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 650 | Gold: | 935 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | All Power Types except Parental | Other Requirements: | None |
| Cheese: | None | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Randomly changes every 24 hours.See Locations section below. | Loot: | Ancient Relic |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| For many years, the Relic Hunter Mouse scoured the Kingdom of Gnawnia in search of precious Ancient Relics and would steal them from unsuspecting hunters wherever she went. At long last, her search has finally completed and she has collected so many Ancient Relics that she can now undertake her ultimate goal of using them to decipher the true origin of mice in Gnawnia and why they came here; an ancient mystery that has been lost to the ages. Now she travels all around the Kingdom, studying the wonders of each place she visits, and using the Ancient Relics as the key to unlocking the secrets of murine prehistory.<br>The Relic Hunter Mouse is restless and obsessive, traveling to a new location every day, as she tries to solve her great mystery. Hunters who are looking to obtain Ancient Relics for their own purposes can attempt to decipher the clues she leaves behind to locate this elusive mouse. Once she's been located, simply hunt in that location and she'll occasionally pass by your trap. She is too preoccupied to bother with your cheese or charm but if you manage to catch her, you'll be able to loot some of her precious Ancient Relics! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 401 |  |  |

## Attracting the Relic Hunter Mouse

Each hunt in the current location of the Relic Hunter Mouse, both through sounding the Hunter's Horn and the hourly trap check, has the potential to attract the Relic Hunter Mouse in addition to any mice that may be attracted to the Hunter's Cheese.
Encountering a Relic Hunter Mouse will not affect progress in any area when encountered.

The attraction of the Relic Hunter Mouse is not affected by any Cheese or Charms.

### Bonus Hunt

A successful catch of the Relic Hunter Mouse will occur as a bonus hunt that does not consume either Cheese or Charms.
The outcome of the main hunt, whether it is a successful catch, failure to catch or failure to attract, has no impact on the outcome of the Relic Hunter Mouse's bonus hunt.

## Locations

Every 24 hours, the Relic Hunter Mouse randomly moves to one of the following locations.
There is a chance for the Relic Hunter Mouse to move to the current location it was at, effectively staying at the same location for more than 24 hours.
Viewing the Treasure Map popup under the Invites and Scroll Cases tab offers a hint to the Relic Hunter's current location.

Note: The Relic Hunter Mouse appears in the Living Garden and Twisted Garden at the same time.

| Region | Location | The Relic Hunter has been spotted... |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gnawnia | Town of Gnawnia | Hiding within the hustle and bustle in the city of the crown.<br>In a town with a dense population.<br>Trying to spot the King himself. |
| Windmill | By an agricultural structure once owned by one of Gnawnia's most prosperous farmers.<br>Grinding up hundreds of tiny seeds from a stalky, golden plant.<br>Observing the churning and grinding of the new harvest. |  |
| Harbour | By the sea where there's plenty of fresh air and sunshine.<br>Near the loud and low horns and the dinging of bells.<br>Visiting where many new hunters seek out seafaring mice. |  |
| Mountain | Cutting through the pass to reach the town on the other side.<br>Looking across vast landscapes and the many horizons of the land.<br>In a treacherous environment where only the toughest of mice survive. |  |
| Valour | King's Arms | Browsing wares available with a most royal currency.<br>Under a circular roof atop arm-shared paths.<br>Where royal strength rewards hunting prowess. |
| Tournament Hall | Amongst the triumphant trumpets of master hunters of old.<br>Browsing the rewards of competitive champions.<br>Competing for the limelight amongst the finest champions. |  |
| King's Gauntlet | Atop a tall tower with the perfect view of an Eclipse.<br>Climbing up spiralling, menacing stairs.<br>Trekking up a massive tower in Valour. |  |
| Whisker Woods | Calm Clearing | By a peaceful rock in a grassy clearing.<br>Taking a relaxing hike through a forested area.<br>Tucked behind dense trees where it's quiet and peaceful. |
| Great Gnarled Tree | By a tree older than Gnawnia itself.<br>Finding shade in the largest tree in the Kingdom.<br>Tracing the deep patterns of bark growing on ancient towers. |  |
| Lagoon | Amongst sparkling, still water.<br>Climbing jagged rocks and slick moss.<br>Waist-deep in a shallow, sparkling pond. |  |
| Burroughs | Laboratory | Amongst brightly glowing potions.<br>Performing bizarre experiments and chemical reactions.<br>Where the powerful and strange breeds of mice first arose. |
| Town of Digby | Amongst powerful drills and excavation equipment.<br>Exploring the deep and winding caverns near a technologically-advanced underground city.<br>Hiding in the shadows while standing in the limelight. |  |
| Mousoleum | Investigating the spirits of slain mice.<br>Studying the spooky remains of Zombie Mice.<br>Surveying where scientists harvest 'spare parts'. |  |
| Bazaar | Ducking between stalls and tents and loud merchants.<br>Searching for the best deals in the Burroughs.<br>Under the pointiest tent in all the Kingdom! |  |

## History and Trivia

- 29 August 2012: The Relic Hunter Mouse is released in the Muridae Market. Its location changed on a predictable weekly basis.
- 6 May 2013: The daily location of Relic Hunter Mouse mouse begins to change randomly.
- 28 April 2013: Catching the Relic Hunter Mouse in the Seasonal Garden begins giving hunters 1% increase in their Tower Amplifier.
- 23 June 2015: The Relic Hunter Mouse stopped dropping Treasure Map Scroll Cases and Living Garden Scroll Cases and began dropping Relic Hunter Scroll Cases as part of Season 3 of treasure hunting.
- 27 July 2016: The Relic Hunter Mouse encounter was changed to a Bonus Hunt that does not consume cheese or charms. The second paragraph of its description was also changed. The previous description read:

> This mouse is so dedicated to the study of Ancient Relics that they'll never approach your trap until you have at least one, and will approach more often if you have more. Further, the Relic Hunter Mouse will only be searching in one location at a time, so you'll have to search if you expect to find any!

- 13 November 2024: The Relic Hunter Mouse has been modified to drop Ancient Relics instead of stealing them in exchange for Relic Hunter Scroll Cases.

> As a result, Hunters no longer require Ancient Relics in their inventory in order to attract the Relic Hunter Mouse.
The description was also changed to reflect this change. The old description read:
From the mountains of Gnawnia to Zugzwang's famous Gardens, the Relic Hunter Mouse leaves no trap unturned in the search for elusive Ancient Relics. Sure, they can be found in the possession of some of the most dangerous mice around, but, well... That's dangerous! It's far safer (relatively) to try to check out the relics that hunters have accrued. And besides, free cheese!

> This mouse is so dedicated to the study of Ancient Relics that she'll never approach your trap until you have at least one. The Relic Hunter Mouse will stay in one location for an entire day before moving on, so you'll have to search Gnawnia to find her every day!

| Once young and lively, this minotaur loved racing through the hallways of the Labyrinth, chasing down hunters and mice alike, howling and bellowing with delight as they scurried at the mere sound of his hooves on the cobbled floors. But now, it seems he has run his last lap of the maze, and has settled down into cozy end-life routines. Donning his fuzzy slippers in his favourite easy chair (which is a giant sack of gold), this retired beast has had his pension paid out in full and has relocated to his secret inner chamber to enjoy his retirement in peace and quiet.<br>The same shenanigans that used to bring him joy now only cause him grief, and he can be seen shaking his fist from atop his tower at the other mice hustling and bustling in the city. All that noise, all that racket! What a grumpy old grump this once playful beast has become...<br>But even in his twilight and seemingly endless misery, he still manages to let a small grin spread across his lips whenever he causes a mouse to jump in fear at the sound of his snort or the clipping of his hooves.<br>No one has broken into his private chambers and lived to tell the tale. Rumor has it that he stores many great and valuable items on opulent displays. Perhaps a resourceful hunter can find a way in and nab one of these rare treasures before being caught! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 782 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

The Retired Minotaur Mouse prefers Glowing Gruyere, but can be attracted with Standard Cheeses.

## Hunting Strategy

Forgotten weapons are very effective against the Retired Minotaur Mouse. Arcane weapons are of normal effectiveness.

The Retired Minotaur Mouse can only be found in the Lair of the Minotaur. While it can be encountered at any time within the Lair of the Minotaur after the Hunter has caught any one mouse, it is more easily attracted and caught as its state (as indicated in the HUD) moves closer to Reckless. Hunters may only catch one Retired Minotaur Mouse per visit to the Lair of the Minotaur.

Hunters are returned to the beginning of the Labyrinth upon catching a Retired Minotaur Mouse.

| Before it was home to a swarm of lich fiends, Balack’s Cove was known for its strange tidal patterns. One moment, the tide is so far out to sea that you can see clams going about their business a mile out, and the next, it rushes back in, swallowing anything caught in the spillover. The source of these tidal quirks is the Riptide Mouse, a mercurial character who is seldom seen, but often felt when its waves wash hapless Hunters up on the sandy shores of the Jungle of Dread. |  |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

Riptide mice have been found to be attracted to both Vanilla Stilton cheese and Vengeful Vanilla Stilton cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

Capturing a Riptide Mouse will cause Hunters to be washed out of Balack's Cove and into the Jungle of Dread.

- During Low Tide and Medium Tide the Riptide Mouse cannot be encountered.
- During High Tide the Riptide Mouse is the only mouse that can be encountered with its preferred cheese.

Arming any of the various Anchor Charms will prevent a Hunter from being washed out when capturing a Riptide Mouse.

## History and Trivia

- 17 January 2023: Riptide Mouse stopped appearing on all Treasure Maps. Riptide Mouse also began to drop Flawless Orb and Scrap Metal as loot.

Forgotten weapons are very effective against the RR-8 Mouse. Arcane weapons are of normal effectiveness.

- Labyrinth

> The RR-8 Mouse can be found in Plain, Superior, and Epic Tech Hallways.

- Zokor

> The RR-8 Mouse can be found in the Tech Foundry Outskirts, the Tech Research Center, and the Manaforge.

## Loot

- Zokor

> Labyrinth Theme Scrap I and Tech Power Cores

## History and Trivia

- 9 September 2015: RR-8 Mouse was released as part of the Hollow Heights.

The Shadow Sage Mouse is a breed of mouse found on the Floating Islands, on a Shadow Stronghold.

| These doyens of the dark arts are said to be as dangerous as they are mysterious. They practice a form of shadow magic so old and so powerful that even most other shadow casters tremble in their presence. There are legends that these sinister sages are older than the very islands on which they live. While other, more outlandish tales, describe them as the ones who created the night itself. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1051 |  |  |

## Cheese Preference

The Shadow Sage Mouse is only attracted to Cloud Cheesecake.

## Hunting Strategy

Only Shadow traps are effective against the Shadow Sage Mouse, all other power types are ineffective. The Shadow Sage Mouse can only be encountered on a Shadow Stronghold

## Loot

### Floating Islands's Island Based Loot

When found on a Low Altitude Island or a High Altitude Island, depending on the buffs present, the Shadow Sage Mouse can drop the following loot:

| Item | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| Sky Glass | Always drops Boosted by Sky Glass Formations and Loot Caches |
| Sky Ore | Always drops Boosted by Sky Ore Deposit and Loot Caches |
| Cloud Curd | Drops when a Cloud Curd Bonus is present Can be boosted by Loot Caches |
| Corsair's Curd | Drops when a Pirate Den is present Can be boosted by Loot Caches |

## History and Trivia

- 08 September 2020: The Shadow Sage Mouse was introduced with the release of the Floating Islands.

## Cheese and Charm Preference

### Cheese

The Shaman Mouse is attracted mainly to Standard Cheese.

In the Calm Clearing location, the Shaman Mouse will also be attracted when hunting with Cherry Cheese.
In the Great Gnarled Tree location, the Shaman Mouse will also be attracted when hunting with Gnarled Cheese.
In the Lagoon location, the Shaman Mouse will not be attracted when hunting with Gnarled Cheese or Wicked Gnarly Cheese.

### Charm

No Charms are required to attract the Shaman Mouse.

| VeryEffective | Effective | Less Effective |

Hunters can encounter the Shaman Mouse in the Calm Clearing, Great Gnarled Tree, andLagoon locations.

The Shaman Mouse drops Splintered Wood in the Calm Clearing, Great Gnarled Tree, andLagoon locations.

## History and Trivia

- 31 March 2009: The Shaman Mouse was released with the introduction of the Calm Clearing.
- 14 April 2011: The Shaman Mouse began dropping the Antique Green Plaid Egg as loot as part of the Spring Egg Hunt 2011 event.
- 25 June 2013: The Shaman Mouse gained a vulnerability to Law traps with the release of Varmint Valley.

| This old, retired, grumpy gus of an engineer has put his yearly plans to travel to warmer climes for the winter on hold. He's usually on a westerly wagon to the Sandtail Desert by now, but the Festive Comet unfortunately landed right on top of his wagon before he boarded. Now, he's a bit stranded and, as you can imagine, a bit cold!<br>This mouse has meticulously planned his retirement around being just the right amount of warm all year; never too hot, and never, ever too cold. So much thought has gone into this lifestyle decision that he has changed his whole wardrobe to revolve around only wearing his favourite summer apparel: Shorts!<br>Stubborn as ever, he has put his engineering know-how (and most of his retirement savings) towards developing quite the sophisticated network of portable heaters to heat things up a bit! Nothing will get in this mouse's way when it comes to enjoying his retirement!<br>He is not letting a little snow ruin his plans for having his fun in the sun this winter, but the sudden rapid heating near the Festive Comet is threatening to thaw the Winter Hunt cheer too early this year and he must be stopped! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1011 |  |  |

## Cheese and Charm Preference

### Cheese

## History and Trivia

- 16 March 2010: The Silth Mouse was released for the first time.
- 25 January 2011: The Silth Mouse began to drop Divine Orbs as loot.
- 22 March 2011: Catching the Silth Mouse became one requirement for gaining the Sandtail Call to Arms which allows travel to the Fiery Warpath. Hunters who had already caught a Silth Mouse did not have to catch another one.
- 14 April 2011: The Silth Mouse began dropping a bonus Silth Egg as loot as part of the annual Spring Egg Hunt event.
- 29 August 2012: The Silth Mouse began dropping Ancient Relics as loot.
- 29 July 2012: Catching the Silth Mouse stopped being a requirement for gaining the Sandtail Call to Arms.
- Originally the Silth Mouse dropped Plankrun's Journal Cover, but this was removed with the upgrade to MouseHunt 3.0.
- In the first month that the Silth Mouse was released, MouseHunt developers hosted a contest to determine the top three hunters who could catch the most of this breed. Prizes were awarded in the amounts of $50 of SUPER|brie+ (3,500 pieces), $25 of SUPER|brie+ (1,600 pieces), and $10 of SUPER|brie+ (500 pieces), respectively.

Their love of shiny objects can, however, be used to a hunter's advantage -- use SUPER|brie+ or Festive Feta and a Snowflake Mouse may visit to investigate your trap. - 30 June 2010: The Speedy Mouse was released with the introduction of the Windmill location.

- 25 March 2014: The Speedy Mouse gained a vulnerability to Rift power type traps, with the introduction of the Rift Plane region.
- 2 September 2014: The Speedy Mouse began dropping Packets of Flour as loot in the Windmill.
- 5 October 2021: The Gold for Speedy Mouse was increased as part of the Town of Gnawnia and Windmill gameplay updates.

Stonework Warrior mice have been found to be especially attracted to Magical Havarti cheese, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice.

Any human who dares to delve into the Elemental Dragons' Den had best prepare themselves for this dragon's intolerant fury! |  |  |  |

Supremia Magnificus is only attracted to Elemental Emmental.

The Supremia Magnificus can only be attracted while hunting in an Elemental Dragons' Den.

Only Draconic power types are effective against Supremia Magnificus.
All other types are ineffective.

- 13 August 2024: Supremia Magnificus was released as part of Draconic Depths location.

| With the methodical moves of a ticking clock, the Technic King pushes his armies into battle, calculating their attacks using cold, hard logic. If this King needs to lose a few pawns to gain the victory, so be it. He's also not afraid to use a little firepower, as evidenced by the secret weapon hiding under his crown. Some people call this mouse fearless, but perhaps he is better understood as a dangerous eccentric; his throne sounds as though it will explode at any second and his crown could probably level the tower. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 269 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

Technic King mice have no specific preference for any kind of cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

The weaknesses of the Technic King Mouse differ slightly from most others in the Wizard's Pieces group. Tactical weapons are very effective against it, while all the others are less effective. It is only available to attract after a Technic Queen mouse has been caught.

Upon capturing a Technic King mouse, the hunter is automatically transported back to the Seasonal Garden unless they are using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm. By using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm a hunter is able to remain in Zugzwang's Tower and attempt to capture additional mice, including the Chess Master.

Upon capturing a Technic King mouse with either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm armed, the mouse population changes. If Checkmate Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Chess Master, Technic Rook and whichever Mystic mice have been unlocked. If Standard Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Technic Pawn and whichever Mystic mice have been unlocked.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Technic King Mouse drops the Technic King Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

## History and Trivia

- Catching the Technic King Mouse became one requirement for traveling to the Fiery Warpath when it was released on 22 March 2011. Hunters who had already caught this mouse did not have to catch another one.
- Technic King mice began dropping the Antique Wavy Purple Egg as loot, on 18 April 2011, for the Spring Egg Hunt 2011 event.
- 29 July 2012: Catching the Technic King Mouse is no longer a requirement for gaining the Sandtail Call to Arms

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

The Menace Mouse is a breed of mouse found in the Toxic Spill, for hunters of rank Grand Duke/Grand Duchess and above.

| The Menace Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: The Polluted |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 125,000 | Gold: | 10,500 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Hydro | Other Requirements: | Grand Duke/Grand Duchess spill level and above requiredonly if using Rancid Radioactive Blue |
| Cheese: | Rancid Radioactive BlueMagical Rancid Radioactive Blue | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Toxic Spill | Loot: | Canister RingCrude PollutinumPolluted Theme Scrap IPolluted Theme Scrap IIPolluted Theme Scrap III |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| With unknown origins, the Menace Mouse seems to be a victim of circumstance. This mouse started appearing shortly after the spills started and is believed to be the direct result of the initial environmental shock caused by the pollution, leading to an immediate and violent mutation.Once mutated, this mouse grows in size, strength and attitude in a matter of minutes! Clearly angered by what has happened to his home, he smashes through the piles of refuse, looking for anything and everything to destroy, fuelled by raw anger amplified by the nearby radiation.Best to stay clear and not to anger him any further. You wouldn't like him when he's angry... |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 527 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

The Menace Mouse can be attracted at every spill level when the Hunter arms Magical Rancid Radioactive Blue.
It can only be attracted at Grand Duke/Grand Duchess spill level and above when the Hunter arms Rancid Radioactive Blue.

## Hunting Strategy

Hydro type traps are effective against The Menace Mouse.

## History and Trivia

- Released on 12 February 2014 as part of the second Toxic Spill content.
- The description of The Menace Mouse contains references to the Hulk comic book character.

## Preferred Cheese

The Thunder Strike has been found to be especially attracted to Dragonvine Cheese cheese, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice.

| VeryEffective | Effective | Less Effective |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | Draconic | None |

Only Draconic type traps are effective against the Thunder Strike, all other power types are ineffective.

Dragonbane Charms, Super Dragonbane Charms and Extreme Dragonbane Charms provide a power bonus against the Thunder Strike.

The Thunder Strike is only available when either wind or rain intensities are between 0%-34% in Moussu Picchu.

- 6 September 2017: The Thunder Strike was introduced as part of the Moussu Picchu release.

Pouring over decades of designs and patterns, this inquisitive mouse began his illustrious career in the world of cloth and thread as a humble tailor, weaving beautiful garments for the mousey elite, inspired by history's influence over fashion.<br>The more he explored the history of fashion, the more he learned its secrets. His first real commission as a professional tailor was to knit a magical scarf for Zugzwang himself. Realizing his talents, he slowly began to grasp the ability to weave the fabric of time itself, which was no simple feat.<br>Key moments in history where fashion had an effect on crucial events began to reveal themselves....<br>The Time Thief Mouse realized that these pivotal points in time would be critical in shifting the balance of power away from hunters and more toward mice, perhaps thinking he could help to relieve their supposed plight. He had no choice but to tear the very fabric of time and step into MouseHunt's past to re-write history...<br>If this mouse succeeds, history as we know it will change and our way of living will cease to exist! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 926 |  |  |

# 🐭 Tiny Mouse

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

> "Tiny" redirects here. For more uses, see Tiny (disambiguation).

The Tiny Mouse is a breed of mouse found in various locations in Gnawnia, and in King's Arms.

| Tiny Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Indigenous Mice (Misc.) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 200 | Gold: | 900 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Any type | Other Requirements: | None |
| Cheese: | Standard CheeseSUPER&#124;brie+ | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | King's ArmsMeadowWindmill | Loot: | Packet of Flour |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| Tiny Mice have two major advantages over larger mice. First of all, a morsel of cheese can feed a Tiny Mouse for more than two weeks, unlike larger mice who gobble the cheese up as soon as they get it. Secondly, when they attack a trap, the weapon often misses them entirely, leaving them free to pursue the cheese. Stubbornness is the only reason Tiny Mice get caught at all. Once they win a piece of cheese, they won’t let it go, even if it’s five times their weight. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 239 |  |  |

## Cheese and Charm Preference

### Cheese

The Tiny Mouse is mainly attracted to SUPER|brie+ in the Meadow location; Brie Cheese and Gouda Cheese may also be used, though the attraction rate will be much lower.
The Tiny Mouse is attracted only to SUPER|brie+ in the King's Arms and Windmill locations.
The Tiny Mouse will not be attracted when hunting with Grilled Cheese in the Windmill location.

### Charm

No Charms are required to attract the Tiny Mouse.

## Power Type Effectiveness

| Very Effective | Effective | Less Effective |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | All except Parental | None |

## Loot

The Tiny Mouse drops Packets of Flour in the Windmill location.

The Tiny Mouse is not known to drop loot in the King's Arms and Meadow locations.

## History and Trivia

- Prior to the release of the Tiny Mouse, it appeared in an error message with this image and the following text:

> The Tiny Mouse's little legs were too slow to fetch your data.
Your profile data timed out while loading.
Please wait a few seconds before reloading the page.

- 30 June 2010: The Tiny Mouse was introduced as part of the Windmill update.
- 14 April 2011: The Tiny Mouse began dropping the Antique Green Plaid Egg as loot in the Meadow as part of the Spring Egg Hunt 2011 event.
- 25 June 2013: The Tiny Mouse gained a vulnerability to Law power type traps, with the release of Varmint Valley.
- 19 September 2013: The Tiny Mouse gained a taste for Brie Cheese and Gouda Cheese during the Gnawnia population shift, although SUPER|brie+ still remains the most effective.
- 25 March 2014: The Micro Mouse was introduced as the Rift counterpart of the Tiny Mouse.
- 25 March 2014: The Tiny Mouse gained a vulnerability to Rift power type traps, with the introduction of the Rift Plane.
- 5 October 2021: The Gold for the Tiny Mouse was increased as part of the Town of Gnawnia and Windmill gameplay update.

# 🐭 Ultimate Mythweaver

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

Ultimate Mythweaver is a breed of mouse found on the in Conclusion Cliffs.

| Ultimate Mythweaver |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Conclusion Cliffhangers (Lore Weavers) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 1,250,000 | Gold: | 225,000 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Law | Other Requirements: |  |
| Cheese: | Plotting PaneerStoried SagaDeus Ex Maconnais | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Conclusion Cliffs | Loot: |  |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| The long and winding road through the Folklore Forest has been wrought with perils both for the MouseHunters and the Mythweaver alike. But alas, all stories must eventually end and this one finds its climax here at the great precipice known as the Conclusion Cliffs.<br>Since his humble beginnings as a lowly Bookborn under the tutelage of Zurreal the Eternal, this aspirational adversary has sought to overthrow the King of Gnawnia and bring about the end of human supremacy. He used the transformative magic of the Folklore Forest to write himself multiple new identities, each with the goal of being the one that would finally defeat the MouseHunters and lead the mice to victory. First he attempted to rewrite history at the Table of Contents and then tried to write himself into all of Gnawnia's great folktales but he was stopped at every turn by the fearless, relentless hunters who pursued him.<br>Now he has finally come to the end of his road at the top of the towering Conclusion Cliffs where the MouseHunters of Gnawnia have backed him into a corner. In his last ditch attempt to fight back, he has split himself into multiple versions based on the five main literary genres. Each version has assembled its own army of mice adapted from the most famous and infamous literary characters of their respective genres. This, the truest and most ultimate form of the Mythweaver, remains protected by the unimaginable power of the greatest genre of all: Fantasy!<br>However, if the hunters can demonstrate their writing prowess by earning Notoriety in all of the main genres then they will prove their ability to write a Fantasy tale so great that the Mythweaver will be unable to resist the challenge. Only then will the MouseHunters finally be able to close the book on this sinister storyteller for good and seal him in a just conclusion for eternity.<br>One loose end that the King's best scholars have been unable to decipher all this time is: how exactly did a meek and meager Bookborn amass profound, devastating, otherworldly power to the extent that it was capable of raising a massive, sprawling army and ravaging an entire region? There is some piece of this puzzle that has yet to be found. Perhaps some force, far greater and more mysterious still, that has played a pivotal role in this malevolent mouse's meteoric rise to power. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1292 |  |  |

## Cheese Preference

Ultimate Mythweaver is attracted to Plotting Paneer or Storied Saga or Deus Ex Maconnais.

## Hunting Strategy

The Ultimate Mythweaver can only be attracted while writing a postscript to a story.

Only Law power types are effective against Ultimate Mythweaver.
All other types are ineffective.

## History and Trivia

- 13 January 2026: Ultimate Mythweaver was released as part of Conclusion Cliffs location.

# 🐭 Unknown Mouse

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

An Unknown Mouse is a mouse that has yet to be caught by a hunter. These mice are usually either new or very rare. Unknown mice are displayed with a placeholder image of a question mark, which is later replaced by a silhouette of the mouse after it has been caught for the first time. Despite being unknown, the MouseHunt Info Page will still provides the power and power type of the mouse. It will also include either a description of the mouse or a note saying that the hunter has not yet discovered a location where the mouse resides.

Once the ship flies within reach, this chilling monstrosity takes one massive swipe with its mighty arms and hurls a barrage of ice and hail with such tremendous force that it can obliterate even the sturdiest of hulls. So many over-zealous treasure seekers have met this icy fate over the centuries that the island elders believe the mountains themselves were built from the frozen remains of ancient airships. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1031 |  |  |

- 9 September 2014: The Zombot Unipire the Third was released as the Rift counterpart of the Zombot Unipire Mouse.

# 🐭 Zombot Unipire the Third

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

The Zombot Unipire the Third is a breed of mouse found in the Burroughs Rift. It is known to drop Terre Ricotta Potion and Brain Bits as loot.

| Zombot Unipire the Third |  |  |  |

| Mouse Group: Rift Walkers (Burroughs Rift) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 45,000 | Gold: | 4,500 |

| Required Power Types: | Rift | Other Requirements: | See below |
| Cheese: | Marble StringSwiss StringBrie StringMagical StringUndead String Emmental | Charm: | None |

| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| The third redesign of the Zombot Unipire is a real looker! His solid steel chassis draped with a red velvet cape is topped with a perfectly synthesized unicorn horn. The horn creates a trail of hopes and dreams that sometimes mesmerize even the unipire himself. Fighting an internal struggle, he was programmed to do bad but wants to do good! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 669 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

Zombot Unipire the Third can be attracted using any Standard String Cheese or Undead String Emmental.

## Hunting Strategy

Zombot Unipire the Third can be attracted by using either:

- Standard String Cheese when the Mist Meter is in Green Zone.
- Undead String Emmental

Using Brain Charm or Super Brain Charm increases the attraction rate of Zombot Unipire the Third.

Rift power type is effective against Zombot Unipire the Third while all others are less effective.

## History and Trivia

- 9 September 2014: The Zombot Unipire the Third was released as part of the Burroughs Rift location.
- 13 January 2015: The Zombot Unipire the Third gained its preference to Brain Charm and Super Brain Charm with the start of Zombie Invasion Week 2015.

# 🐭 Zurreal the Eternal

> **Entity**: Mouse_lore

> "Zurreal" redirects here. For other uses, see Zurreal (disambiguation).

Zurreal the Eternal is a breed of mouse found in the Crystal Library. It is known to drop Reaper's Perch Blueprints and Ancient Relic as loot.

| Zurreal the Eternal |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Zurreal's Breed |  |  |  |

| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| Madness and the desire for power is enough to drive most bad mice to villainous acts against humans; however, Zurreal took his greed much further, turning even on his own kind.<br>Zurreal is the only known living mouse to make it into the library through Zugzwang's protective enchantments. The process of passing through the powerful shields nearly killed this relentless mouse, but in the end it could not stop him.<br>Once inside, he began his devious plot to steal all of the knowledge of the library, destroy the research and then use the boundless knowledge as a weapon against humans and mice alike.<br>Through his gathering of power it has been speculated that he may be unstoppable, as countless hunters have claimed to have captured him, only for another hunter to exclaim the same thing.<br>He has no known allies aside from the magical and technological creations that surround him, who aide in his dark and seemingly eternal task. If you can capture this mouse, even just to set his dark plans back, surely the reward will be great. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 344 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

Zurreal the Eternal can be attracted using any Standard Cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

Zurreal the Eternal can only be attracted with a Scholar Charm armed.

Zurreal's Folly is the only effective weapon against Zurreal the Eternal.

## History and Trivia

- 23 August 2011: Zurreal the Eternal was introduced on 23 August 2011 and was first caught by hunters two days later.
- It was the 3rd mouse to be introduced that required a specific charm to be armed in order to attract it, after Blacksmith and Mage Weaver in Muridae Market.
- 29 August 2012: Zurreal the Eternal began dropping Ancient Relic as loot.

# ⚔️ 10 Layer Birthday Cake Base

> **Entity**: Equipment | **Element**: General | **Rank**: Novice

> **Classification**: General Base  
> **Power / Luck**: 300 Power | 10 Luck  
> **Title Requirement**: Novice  
> **Acquisition Cost**: 0

## 📜 Lore & Rekayasa Perangkap

> A 10-layer birthday cake has been baked right into this limited edition base to celebrate 10 years of MouseHunt!
> Over the last 10 years, the kitchen floors of the castle have seen their fair share of leftovers and table scraps. Slowly, as the years went on, and birthday cake after birthday cake was baked in The King's Grand Birthday Cake Oven, small remnants and pieces of cakes from years passed collected along the edges of and below the main cooking surface.
> The final result? This utter masterpiece, lovingly scraped from the insides of the oven, held together by the strongest known frosting to the Kingdom to ensure perfect cohesion. Carefully stenciled by hand onto each piece is a sweet birthday message to forever remember this moment.
> Oh, and of course, being comprised of the very same chunks of cake made for previous birthdays, this base comes with every known special effect present on other birthday cake bases! Namely, the special effects of the various cupcake bases.
> Happy 10th Birthday, MouseHunters!

## 🔨 Asal-Usul & Perakitan (Crafting/Shoppe)
The 10 Layer Birthday Cake Base was a reward for completing the Restore_Gnawnia's_10-Year_Timeline adventure during The_Grand_Time_Tampering event.

It was designed by the greatest lapidary ever to roam the clouds. The craftsman's name has unfortunately been lost to the ages but their work lives on as a powerful tool to rid the skies of vermin.
> In addition to its extraordinary mouse-catching power, this miracle of modern science has the following special effect:

# ⚔️ Alchemist's Cookbook Base

> **Entity**: Equipment | **Element**: General | **Rank**: Recruit

> **Classification**: General Base  
> **Power / Luck**: 350 Power | 10 Luck  
> **Title Requirement**: Recruit  
> **Acquisition Cost**: See below

## 📜 Lore & Rekayasa Perangkap

> This dark and mystical tome once belonged to Baba Gaga, the wretched witch of the Gloomy Greenwood. Its pages are filled with her most terrifying potion recipes and in the wrong hands could surely do immeasurable harm. However, when wielded by a brave and noble hunter, this enchanted text has the tremendous ability to occasionally reproduce any potion that enters its sphere of influence.
> This base has a chance to duplicate any potion that a mouse drops as loot.
> When armed with the Boiling Cauldron Trap, this base is guaranteed to duplicate any potion that the trap produces.
> When armed in the Gloomy Greenwood, this base is guaranteed to duplicate any potion dropped from mice.

- 2021: from the Reward Track after brewing 10 batches of Evil Extract.
